mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior 5-quarter average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-quarter moving average
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from a constant mean (Granger causality p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS increase is not persistent (5-quarter MA persistence < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above its 4-week moving average while HOUST falls below its 4-week moving average
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market weakening in a growth slowdown
failure_condition: Over 200-day window, SPX 60-day returns are positive in >70% of similar labor signal events (bootstrap); or correlation between PAYEMS/HOUST and SPX 60d returns is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals economic expansion and equity risk appetite.
regime_hint: Recovery phase following a contractionary period
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive 20-day windows with INDPRO acceleration, SPX 20d returns are not statistically superior to a baseline (bootstrap p > 0.05); or INDPRO acceleration is not predictive after controlling for CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS (multivariate Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in goods orders (RSAFS) below the prior 3-month average coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates future supply-side shocks.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below its 3-month moving average
failure_condition: Over 100 events with RSAFS contraction, SPX 5-day returns are not systematically negative (bootstrap p > 0.1); or RSAFS contraction is not predictive after controlling for UNRATE and HOUST (multivariate Granger p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% and coincides with a sustained decline in CPIAUCSL inflation (monthly), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 60-day forward returns as markets anticipate a prolonged low-inflation environment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and CPIAUCSL declines for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such regimes, SPX 60d returns are not statistically higher than a control group (bootstrap p > 0.05); or UNRATE/CPIAUCSL relationship is not predictive after controlling for FEDFUNDS (multivariate Granger p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (PAYEMS) above 8 million coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor market conditions boost equity valuations.
regime_hint: Labor market loosening in a growth environment
failure_condition: In 50 such events, SPX 20d returns are not statistically positive (bootstrap p > 0.05); or PAYEMS strength is not predictive after controlling for HOUST and INDPRO (multivariate Granger p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not available in the provided proxies; fallback to HOUST as proxy for consumer demand) and a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) predict a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as demand destruction accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below prior month's value and INDPRO falls below prior month's value
regime_hint: Demand destruction in a recessionary setup (proxy interpretation)
failure_condition: Over 40 such dual-contraction events, SPX 5d returns are not systematically negative (bootstrap p > 0.1); or the interaction is not significant after controlling for FEDFUNDS (multivariate Granger p > 0.1).
